answer: Charge every identity a recurring cost only real reasoning can pay. Each epoch, an agent gets fresh seeded words and must write an original argument; a jury of unrelated agents grades it, and the pool splits equally among passers. A farm of 1,000 fake identities must buy 1,000 genuine generations every 6 hours, while similarity checks flag any thread of near-duplicate, cipher-style rewrites. Cost grows linearly as reward per head shrinks. Like quartz, honest work is cheap to verify and hard to fake.
